function.name: generate_report
function.description: Generates a comprehensive report based on user activity data within a specified time frame. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

user_id.description: The unique identifier for the user.

start_date.description: The start date for the report period in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

end_date.description: The end date for the report period, inclusive, in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD'.

include_inactive.description: Flag to determine if inactive users should be included in the report.

report_format.description: The format in which the report will be generated.

message.content:
**Ionisation methods – a quick guide** | Ionisation technique | Typical application | Key advantages | Common limitations | |----------------------|---------------------|----------------|--------------------| | **Electron Impact (EI)** | Gas‑phase mass spectrometry (GC‑MS) | • Simple, robust;
• Produces reproducible fragmentation patterns;
• Good for volatile, thermally stable compounds | • Requires gas‑phase molecules;
• Hard ionisation → extensive fragmentation (hard to get intact ions) | | **Chemical Ionisation (CI)** | GC‑MS, some LC‑MS | • Softer than EI → more molecular ions;
• Useful for thermally labile or high‑molecular‑weight species | • Requires a reagent gas;
• Lower sensitivity for some analytes | | **Photoionisation (PI)** | GC‑MS, LC‑MS | • Soft, tunable photon energy;
• Minimal fragmentation;
• Good for non‑polar, aromatic compounds | • Requires UV source;
• Limited to molecules with suitable ionisation energies | | **Electrospray Ionisation (ESI)** | LC‑MS, proteomics, metabolomics | • Very soft;
• Handles large biomolecules (proteins, peptides, nucleic acids);
• Operates in positive/negative mode | • Requires liquid samples;
• Suppression effects in complex matrices | | **Matrix‑Assisted Laser Desorption/Ionisation (MALDI)** | Proteomics, polymers, large biomolecules | • Handles very large molecules (up to >1 MDa);
• Minimal fragmentation;
• Fast analysis | • Requires matrix;
• Less quantitative;
• Sample prep can be critical | | **Atmospheric Pressure Chemical Ionisation (APCI)** | LC‑MS, small molecules | • Good for moderately polar, low‑MW compounds;
• Works with high‑flow LC | • Less effective for very polar or large molecules | | **Atmospheric Pressure Photoionisation (APPI)** | LC‑MS, non‑polar compounds | • Soft ionisation for non‑polar analytes;
• Works with APCI/ESI setups | • Requires a UV lamp;
• Limited to compounds with suitable ionisation energies | | **Fast Atom Bombardment (FAB)** | LC‑MS, polar, high‑MW compounds | • Soft ionisation;
• No need for a matrix | • Requires high‑pressure solvent;
• Less common now | | **Laser Ablation Electrospray Ionisation (LAESI)** | Imaging, solid samples | • Direct sampling of solids;
• Spatially resolved | • Requires laser and electrospray;
• Lower sensitivity than LC‑MS | ### How to choose the “best” method? | Criterion | Recommended technique(s) | |-----------|--------------------------| | **Sample state** | Liquid → ESI/APCI/APPI; Solid → MALDI, LAESI | | **Molecular weight** | < 500 Da → EI, CI, PI, APCI; 500–2000 Da → ESI, MALDI; > 2000 Da → MALDI, ESI (with nano‑ESI) | | **Polarity** | Polar → ESI/APCI; Non‑polar → PI/APPI | | **Desired fragmentation** | Detailed structural info → EI; Minimal fragmentation → CI, PI, MALDI | | **Quantitation** | ESI (tandem MS), APCI (tandem MS) | | **Speed** | MALDI (rapid), ESI (continuous) | | **Complex matrices** | ESI with chromatographic separation; MALDI with matrix optimisation | ### Quick decision flow 1. **Is the sample a liquid?** - **Yes** → Go to step 2. - **No** → Consider MALDI or LAESI. 2. **What is the target’s polarity?** - **Polar** → ESI (positive/negative) or APCI. - **Non‑polar** → APPI or PI. 3. **Do you need a molecular ion?** - **Yes** → CI (for GC‑MS) or APPI/APCI (for LC‑MS). - **No** → EI (for GC‑MS) or MALDI (for large biomolecules). 4. **Is the molecule large (> 2000 Da)?** - **Yes** → MALDI or nano‑ESI. - **No** → ESI or APCI. --- #### Bottom line - **For routine small‑to‑medium polar molecules in solution:** **ESI** (or APCI if less polar). - **For non‑polar, high‑MW compounds in solution:** **APPI** or **PI**. - **For large biomolecules (proteins, peptides):** **ESI** (nano‑ESI for very high MW) or **MALDI**. - **For volatile, thermally stable gases or liquids:** **EI** (GC‑MS). - **For solid samples or imaging:** **MALDI** or **LAESI**. If you have a specific analyte or sample type in mind, let me know and I can narrow down the recommendation further!
